why_triggered: A DRAFT fired because the mfg-activity signal moved from 26.7 to -0.4, a -27.1 point change. The trigger reasons were direction_flip and magnitude_step>=25.

signal_findings.what_changed: The Philadelphia Fed current general activity diffusion index moved from 26.7 in April 2026 to -0.4 in May 2026, a -27.1 point move. The May report says regional manufacturing activity weakened overall, and current activity, new orders, and shipments all fell sharply.
signal_findings.what_it_means: This is a sharp cooling, not a deep collapse. A diffusion index is the share of firms reporting increases minus the share reporting decreases, so a reading near zero means increases and decreases were almost balanced. In May, almost 23 percent of firms reported higher activity, almost 23 percent reported lower activity, and 55 percent reported no change. New orders fell to -1.7 and shipments fell to 4.9, so the demand side looked weaker. Employment stayed slightly negative at -2.8. Price pressure eased from April but stayed high, with prices paid at 47.9 and prices received at 26.3. Future activity rose to 53.2, so firms were still optimistic about the next six months.
signal_findings.magnitude_context: The one-month drop of 27.1 points is rare in the Philadelphia Fed historical file. Using seasonally adjusted current general activity data from May 1968 through May 2026, there are 696 month-to-month changes; only eight drops were larger than this one, making the May 2026 drop the ninth-largest decline in that history. The level of -0.4 is close to the zero line, not close to the historical low of -58.7 in April 2020. It sits around the lower 27 percent of monthly readings in the same history.
uncertainties: The Philadelphia Fed notes that seasonally adjusted historical values can be revised after annual seasonal-factor updates, so exact historical rankings may shift slightly.
The survey is regional and qualitative. It measures the breadth of change, not the dollar size or production volume of the change.
The task value and the Philadelphia Fed May report agree on the 26.7 to -0.4 move, but FRED page content did not expose the latest observation values in the fetched page text.

cross_signal_impacts.impact: The regional-national gap framing still has support. The Philly Fed current activity index fell to -0.4 in May, while the S&P Global US Manufacturing PMI rose to 55.1 in May from 54.5 in April and stayed above its 50.0 no-change mark. This suggests the weak Philly reading should not be treated as the whole U.S. factory story.

product_implications.implication: Treat Mid-Atlantic factory demand as more fragile, not broken. If your product sells into plants, some buyers may slow new orders, choose smaller rollouts, or downgrade needs before they cancel. Build sales-assist flows that flag order softness early and offer lower-risk pilots, phased seats, or cost-control workflows before renewal talks.
product_implications.audience: PMs and product operators serving Mid-Atlantic manufacturers
